summary: This document registers the application/sql media type for the Structured Query Language (SQL). Registering it gives software a standard label for SQL content when it is sent or stored.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC registers application/sql as a label for SQL content. It also explains when senders may use the optional charset parameter.

questions: what is the media type for sql
when can application sql use a charset parameter
what security issues apply to sql files
subtitle: Registers application/sql as the media type for Structured Query Language content.

tldr.problem: SQL had been used for decades without a registered media type to identify SQL content.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers application/sql and specifies an optional charset parameter and handling rules for character-set information.
tldr.outcome: IANA registered application/sql in the Application Media Types registry.

today: RFC 6922 is an Informational registration of application/sql in the IANA Application Media Types registry.

sections.title: A Media Type for SQL
sections.content:
Structured Query Language (SQL) had been used with database technologies for over 30 years, but the memo says no media type had been registered for it. RFC 6922 provides the registration application for application/sql.

The document uses the registration process described in RFC 6838 and records application as the type and sql as the subtype.
sections.plainLanguage: SQL did not have an official media type before this registration. The new label is application/sql.

sections.title: Character Sets and Encoding
sections.content:
The registration defines an optional charset parameter. If the charset is not specified, a default must not be assumed without inspecting the content.

SQL may carry charset information in-band; in that case, the charset parameter must not be used to avoid conflict. If no in-band or out-of-band charset information is available, senders must not specify the parameter.
sections.plainLanguage: The charset parameter is optional, but senders must follow the rules for in-band character-set information. Receivers should not assume a default without checking the content.

sections.title: Security and Interoperability
sections.content:
The RFC warns that SQL can include source code for other programming languages and may be used to transfer malicious payloads. It recommends exchanging SQL files only among trusted parties and using available security measures.

SQL does not provide confidentiality or integrity protection, and files may expose account or database information. The memo also notes that vendor implementations vary, so users should check that files fit their database and tool versions.
sections.plainLanguage: SQL files can contain harmful commands and private database details. The format does not protect a file from disclosure or modification.
